About FlyLab 3D

Explore anatomy and practice virtual dissections on adult female and third-instar larval Drosophila melanogaster.

About the Researcher

MA

Muhammad Atif

Researcher & FlyLab 3D Developer

Affiliation
Kookmin University, Seoul, South Korea
Field
Drosophila Research, Molecular Biology, and Neurobiology

Muhammad Atif is a graduate researcher at Kookmin University, South Korea, specializing in Drosophila melanogaster as a model organism. His research interests include insect chemosensation, gustatory receptor mechanisms, neurobiology, molecular genetics, and behavioral physiology. He is interested in integrating experimental biology with interactive 3D technologies to make scientific research techniques more accessible, engaging, and educational for students and researchers.

Model and methods

The 3D geometry is an original educational reconstruction informed by published morphology and organ anatomy. Positions and shapes are schematic. Scientific mode illustrates observed types of grooming and locomotion. Playful poses are expressive animations.

Protocol library

The virtual lessons teach bench preparation, landmark recognition, and dissection sequence. They are educational prototypes awaiting expert review. The linked papers and JoVE pages contain the published methods and videos.

Training plans and session records are saved in this browser when local storage is available.

Observations

Experiment and Compare read CSV or JSON files in your browser. Measurements are averaged by structure, condition and time point. The example file contains illustrative values.
